title: Eritrean-Ethiopian Sweet Bread
community: Northern Ethiopia and Eritrea — the wheel-shaped sweet bread
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Himbasha — the round, wheel-patterned slightly sweet Eritrean and Ethiopian bread. Very similar to Ambasha but with a distinctive wheel or sun-ray pattern cut into the surface and a slightly different spice balance using cardamom and anise alongside fenugreek.
longDesc: Himbasha is the bread that crosses the Ethiopian-Eritrean boundary most comfortably — deeply beloved on both sides, made the same way by both communities, and carried to every corner of the diaspora. The wheel pattern on its surface is both decorative and functional — it creates a ready-made score for breaking the bread into portions.
ingredients: ½ tsp ground anise or fennel
1 tbsp black sesame seeds (optional — scattered on top)
steps: Dissolve yeast and 1 tsp sugar in warm water. Rest 10 minutes.
Combine flour, remaining sugar, salt, and all spices.
Add yeast mixture and oil. Knead 8 minutes.
Press into a large round 2cm thick.
Cut wheel pattern: score from centre to edge like spokes of a wheel — 8 cuts. Then score a circle midway.
Cook in a covered pan on medium-low heat: 20 minutes per side.
chefTips: The anise is the distinguishing spice between himbasha and ambasha.
Score more deeply than you think — the pattern expands during cooking.
cookingScience: See ETH005 for pattern science. The anise in himbasha contains anethole — a highly fragrant compound that is significantly more volatile than fenugreek's sotolone, producing a more immediately intense fragrance when the bread is hot.
sustainabilityTips: Anise and fenugreek grow in Ethiopia — locally produced spices.
culturalNote: Himbasha is the bread that unites Ethiopians and Eritreans in the diaspora — regardless of political boundaries, both communities recognise and cherish this bread as home. At Ethiopian and Eritrean coffee ceremonies worldwide, himbasha is almost always present.
